beats.text: Medical segmentation needs two things at once: the **big picture**, and the exact **edge**.
A U-Net sees edges, but only **locally**. A transformer sees everything, but its cost grows with the **square** of the number of pixels.
Mamba reads the image as a **sequence**, so its cost grows only **linearly**. But it knows nothing about **objects**.
SAM knows objects, because it has seen a huge number of photos. But skin and CT scans look **nothing** like those photos.
The new paper, SAMBA-UNet, runs **both**, and lets SAM guide Mamba.
On the Synapse CT dataset it reports a Dice of **81.94**, against **81.08** for VM-UNet.
That is a gain of under one point, so we will look at it **carefully**.
